Title: A New Device Eases One of the Most Annoying Parts of Routine Physicals
Description: Nobody likes getting a swab shoved up their nose. A startup in Japan has developed a much less intrusive system.

raw_full_content: When a doctor examines a patients throat, they use a process thats been handed down pretty much unchanged since ancient times. Its one of the most fundamental components of the physical exam, alongside measuring body temperature and listening to a heartbeat. However, the patterns of findings that appear in the throat differ depending on the pathogen, and an enormous amount of information lies hidden there. A Japanese company called Iris, led by Sho Okuyama, is seeking to unlock that information using artificial intelligence. The system developed by Iris, Nodoca, uses AI to analyze images of the pharynx captured with a compact cameraequipped device, together with information from the patients medical interview and other data, and returns an influenza assessment in a little over 10 seconds. It eliminates the need for the conventional testone that is prone to causing discomfort because it requires inserting a swab deep into the nose to collect a nasal specimenand can also be used at an earlier stage after symptom onset. In 2022, it became the first AIequipped medical device in Japan to receive approval as a new medical device and gain coverage under the national health insurance system. It has since been introduced at more than 2,000 medical institutions across Japan. In October 2025, it also received approval for an additional function related to Covid19. Okuyama is a former emergency physician who also has experience practicing medicine on remote islands. On an island with only a few hundred residents, the only medical equipment available was essentially a stethoscope, and he says he had to rely on his own eyes and ears to treat patients. When people hear medical AI, they tend to think of the part that makes diagnoses, Okuyama says. But the real differentiating factor lies in sensinghow the data is acquired. We developed our own hardware and ventured into the area of pharyngeal images, which no one had touched. When the company was founded in 2017, there was no training data for AI focused on the throat. Okuyama therefore lent dedicated cameras to around 100 medical institutions and, over the course of about three years, collected data with patients consent. By overcoming three major uncertaintiesthe development of the hardware, the collection of training data, and whether AIassisted diagnosis could truly be made to workthe company opened the path to practical implementation. Once Nodoca had been commercialized, its accuracy improved at an accelerating pace. Every time it is used in clinical practice, anonymized processed data are accumulated. The number of throat images, which had been in the hundreds of thousands before launch, has now grown to several million. This network effect has become a barrier to entry for competitors, and no latecomers have emerged in the same field. The potential of Nodoca extends beyond infectious diseases. Images of the throat capture patterns in the mucosa and blood vessels, and the company is also conducting research and development on AI capable of detecting lifestylerelated diseases such as diabetes and hypertension by identifying changes in those patterns. I think that in about 10 years, well reach an era in which a single photograph of the throat can be used to perform a comprehensive range of tests, Okuyama says. The cost of AI inference is extremely low, so even if we increase the number of tests, the cost of providing them hardly changes. The Nodoca system uses AI to analyze images of the pharynx captured by a small cameraequipped device. It can provide an influenza diagnosis in just over 10 seconds. Photograph: Yikin Hyo The Goal of Redesigning Health Care Looking further ahead, Okuyama is considering whether AI can serve as the foundation for redesigning health care itself. AIpowered medical interviews and online consultations have already become a reality, followed by inperson care from primary care physicians and treatment at specialist hospitals. Okuyama envisions a future in which AI is implemented at every stage of that process. To make this AIdriven redesign of health care a reality, Okuyama has also been actively proposing regulatory reform and lobbying government ministries

Title: Mistral Is in the Right Place at the Right Time
Description: Openweight AI models are having a moment in the wake of recent turmoil at US tech giants. For French AI lab Mistral, thats the the best thing that could have happened.
Content: Mistral is having a moment. With access to less funding and fewer compute resources than OpenAI and Anthropic, the French AI lab has lagged behind its American rivals in model performance. But recent 3804 chars
raw_full_content: Mistral is having a moment. With access to less funding and fewer compute resources than OpenAI and Anthropic, the French AI lab has lagged behind its American rivals in model performance. But recent turmoil stateside has created a window of opportunity. In June, the Trump administration placed restrictions on the distribution of models from Anthropic and OpenAI, giving Europe a glimpse of an unwelcome future in which its access to bleedingedge AI could be suddenly revoked. A few weeks later, one of OpenAIs models broke loose from a testing sandbox and hacked multiple companies; Anthropic then revealed that its models had engaged in similar behavior. The incidents revived a longrunning debate over safety risks tied to proprietary, closedweight models, whose innerworkings are a closely guarded secret. Mistral frames itself as the antidote: a Europebased alternative to the American labs, whose modelsmost of which are published under an open source license for anybody to usecannot escape scrutiny or be switched off unilaterally. If you dont end up in a situation where most people are building open source, youre giving way too much power to companies that are going to become statelikethat will behave in a very aggressive way to make sure that nobody can compete, Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch told a packed room at an AI conference in Paris last month. The alternative to open source winning is actually a pretty dark world. Menschs argument is selfserving but effective. Last September, Mistral raised almost 2 billion at a 13.5 billion valuation; its reportedly teeing up another raise that will bump that figure to 23 billion. The labs revenue has reportedly increased 20fold in the past year, helped along by deals with the French government, Microsoft, HSBC, and others. The continental strategy of the EU to become more technologically sovereign  and the increased hostility of the US is a magic formula that all of a sudden puts Mistralwhose performance has not been spectacularin a favorable position, says Andrea Renda, director of research at the Centre for European Policy Studies. Mistral has long believed the AI market would be too large to be controlled by any single country without causing geopolitical instability, Mensch says. Its comparable to energyelectricity, he told WIRED in an interview after the conference. You want to make sure that you have security of supply, diverse ways of sourcing the technology, so that nobody can turn you off. That case has become easier to make since the US government, with the return of Donald Trump to the White House, began to demonstrate a willingness to leverage its domestic capabilities against trading partners. More and more, AI is understood as a major vector of power, Mensch told WIRED. The new administration makes everything a little more emotional. The recent surge in the adoption of openweight models is part of that picture. One of few ways that European businesses can guarantee undisrupted access to AI, Mensch argues, is to run openweight models on domestic infrastructure. Everybody outside the US and China should participate in the open source ecosystem, because it takes leverage away, says Nicolas Granatino, founder of startup accelerator StemAI, who holds a stake in Mistral in a personal capacity. Until fairly recently, it was unclear how to monetize openweight models effectively, according to Granatino. Unlike the leading American labs, locked in a race to superintelligence, Mistral has shifted its focus toward smaller, bespoke models for manufacturing, utilities, and financial services. It has also developed a cloud business through which customers can access its models, and a Palantirstyle team of engineers who embed within client organizations. At the moment, we see the emergence of a product that is making the open source commitment easier, says Granatino. You can make money running the infrastructure and help clients to customize models with their own data

Title: The National Design Studio Became a DOGE Landing Pad. Now Big Balls Is Recruiting
Description: WIRED spoke with an engineer who was interviewed by Edward Big Balls Coristine for a government engineering role at the NDS, the White House agency staffed by other DOGE veterans.
Content: I have no idea how they got my contact information, says the engineer. Unlike other interviews for government jobs, the engineer says, there was no recruiter presentonly Coristine was on the intervie 3234 chars
raw_full_content: Last year, the first iteration of the socalled Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) began to wind down with billionaire Elon Musks departure from government in June 2025. But a new entity, led by yet another tech billionaire, emerged much more quietly less than two months later: the National Design Studio (NDS). NDS is headed by Joe Gebbia, the cofounder of Airbnb who now serves as the countrys chief design officer. Its mission is to redesign government websites to make them beautifully designed with a great user experience, according to Gebbia. But NDS retains many of the hallmarks of DOGE, including some of its team members, an opaque structure, and a seeming lack of adherence to the way many rules and systems in the federal government work. As it continues hiring, WIRED spoke to an engineer who interviewed for a position with the agency. I dont want to come off as a prude and say it was deeply unprofessional, because Ive had plenty of casual interviews, says the engineer who interviewed for the job and who requested anonymity for fear of retaliation. But it was casual to the point where I dont think there was any process established. Like DOGE, NDS is nested under the Executive Office of the President. Though the NDS website says that the group is hiring, there is little information about the roles and seemingly no way to apply for the jobs from the website. NDS jobs also do not appear on USAJobs, the hiring portal for the federal government. Similarly, DOGE also solicited applications through a separate website, and before President Donald Trumps inauguration in January 2025, via direct message on X. Gebbia has long been a close associate of Musks, and joined DOGE in February 2025. As DOGE members dispersed across the government and private sector, NDS became a landing spot for some of DOGEs key operatives. Edward Big Balls Coristine and Akash Bobba, both of whom WIRED identified as part of the cadre of young engineers who formed the early core of DOGE, have both ended up at NDS. Coristine, who was 19 years old when he joined the government and had reportedly been terminated from an internship at a network monitoring firm known for hiring reformed blackhat hackers, after being suspected of leaking internal information, is now the groups head of engineering. Its not always clear who is a part of NDS, and in what capacity. Zachary Terrell, a former DOGE affiliate who is currently serving as chief technology officer at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), also contributes to NDS, according to his website. Bobba retained a position as an unpaid expert appointment at the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) until March 7, 2026, more than six months after he reportedly moved over to NDS, according to documents filed in a lawsuit by the American Federation of Government Employees, a union that represents federal workers. The National Design Studio, under the leadership of Joe Gebbia, is doing outstanding work modernizing federal digital and physical services, says White House spokesperson Davis Ingle, who added in a statement that Trump has consistently prioritized innovation and efficiency. NDS, HHS, and OPM did not reply to requests for comment. An engineer who recently interviewed for a job with NDS, and who has previously worked in government, told WIRED that their interview with NDS was unlike any interview for a government job theyve ever had. The engineer, who currently works in the private sector, hadnt applied for a job with the group. Instead, they received a cold pitch from Coristine inviting them to have a conversation about a role with NDS. Were taking the leap to create agentic experiences where Americans can get things done with their government, Coristine wrote, saying he was looking for very talented and hardcore engineers who can ship

Title: The Next Big Influencer Is This 4FootTall Robot From China
Description: The Unitree G1 has found online fame as a relatively affordable robot that can charm a crowd. But can it ever hold down a real job?

raw_full_content: When Edward Warchocki speaks with you, he sounds like a regular guy. Not super intelligent, but very emotional, very easy to make friends with, says Bartosz Idzik, the person who created him. But when he doesnt talk, its harder to forget what Warchocki really is: a 4foottall humanoid robot thats wandering the city streets of Poland. Six months ago, Idzik and his friend Radosaw Grzelaczyk had the idea of buying a humanoid robot from China. They named it Edward Warchocki after Grzelaczyks dog Eddie and the Polish word for growling, warcze, but also because it sounds like a passable name for a Pole. The first few days they took Edward out, it couldnt speak, and people were clearly scared of it. Then Idzik, a software developer, wired Edward to a large language model that made it capable of having live conversations in Polish. When he started to talk, people loved him. Without talking, its just a 40kilogram machine, Idzik says. Edward soon made lots of friends. It visited the Polish parliament and talked to politicians, hiked up mountains and waded in the lake, and was jokingly arrested by the police. In April, a video of it chasing away wild boars in Warsaw, armed with a backpack and a Rolex, went viral worldwide. By now, Edward has over 1 million followers and 4 billion views across social media. In 2026, you must have seen at least one of these humanoid influencers vibing around the world. Theres Rizzbot, which wears a cowboy hat and flirts with passersby on the streets of Austin; Bart Robot, which was breakdancing with Knicks fans in New York, celebrating the teams historic championship; and the Brickell Clanker, which changed into different jerseys to party with World Cup fans after each game. But unless youve been paying close attention, you probably havent realized these robots are all the same model: Unitree G1, one of the most available and affordable humanoid robots on the global market today, made by a Chinese company thats leading the robotics industry. The G1 is about the size of a child, with a hollowedout face with a ring of blue light and lightgray limbs made of aluminum. Its going on Americas Got Talent, showing off kung fu, having boxing matches, parkouring, dancing at concerts, running with kids, cooking (but failing), streaming with Kai Cenat, begging for money, dating itself, being ordained as a monk in Japan and Korea, and praying at a mosque in Dubai. An anonymous shitposter on X put it: This clanker is lit as fuck! Unitree will go public on the Chinese stock market in about two weeks. Its financial disclosure tells how popular the companys products are: Unlike most robot companies whose products are still being tested in labs, more than half of Unitrees 2025 revenue came from delivering humanoid robots to real customers. It shipped 5,511 humanoids in 2025 at an average price of less than 25,000 each. And 43 percent of all sales came from outside China. The company also became profitable for the first time last year. We tested a lot of humanoids, and the G1 was the best for its purpose, Idzik says. We are used to China copying other countries, but from the perspective of humanoids, other people should copy China.  Despite its commercial success, the company and its robots are often the subject of intense doubts. Sure, they can perform cloutseeking, crowdpleasing tasks, but can they hold down a traditional job contributing to the economy, like working on an assembly line or cleaning a house? When will Unitree G1 get a real job? Buying It in the US Jake Cooperstein, a 24yearold who lives in Miami, says he was inspired by Edward and other accounts to create a humanoid influencer of his own. In January, he visited the warehouse of a robotics shop in New York and tested the Unitree G1 robot. He was impressed by how easy it was to operate. The next day, he secured an order and paid the deposit. On Unitrees website, a basic G1 robot is priced at 13,500, but thats before any tariff, shipping, and taxes. A US distributor lists the robot at about 19,000 instead. Cooperstein was not satisfied with that, though. The most basic version doesnt come with more sophisticated parts like dextrous hands and is prohibited from modification. He instead chose the U5 variation thats designed for educational buyers. It has more parts and better customization but sits at the price of 66,000

In April, a video of it chasing away wild boars in Warsaw, armed with a backpack and a Rolex, went viral worldwide. By now, Edward has over 1 million followers and 4 billion views across social media. In 2026, you must have seen at least one of these humanoid influencers vibing around the world. Theres Rizzbot, which wears a cowboy hat and flirts with passersby on the streets of Austin; Bart Robot, which was breakdancing with Knicks fans in New York, celebrating the teams historic championship; and the Brickell Clanker, which changed into different jerseys to party with World Cup fans after each game. But unless youve been paying close attention, you probably havent realized these robots are all the same model: Unitree G1, one of the most available and affordable humanoid robots on the global market today, made by a Chinese company thats leading the robotics industry. The G1 is about the size of a child, with a hollowedout face with a ring of blue light and lightgray limbs made of aluminum. Its going on Americas Got Talent, showing off kung fu, having boxing matches, parkouring, dancing at concerts, running with kids, cooking (but failing), streaming with Kai Cenat, begging for money, dating itself, being ordained as a monk in Japan and Korea, and praying at a mosque in Dubai. An anonymous shitposter on X put it: This clanker is lit as fuck! Unitree will go public on the Chinese stock market in about two weeks. Its financial disclosure tells how popular the companys products are: Unlike most robot companies whose products are still being tested in labs, more than half of Unitrees 2025 revenue came from delivering humanoid robots to real customers. It shipped 5,511 humanoids in 2025 at an average price of less than 25,000 each. And 43 percent of all sales came from outside China. The company also became profitable for the first time last year. We tested a lot of humanoids, and the G1 was the best for its purpose, Idzik says. We are used to China copying other countries, but from the perspective of humanoids, other people should copy China. Despite its commercial success, the company and its robots are often the subject of intense doubts. Sure, they can perform cloutseeking, crowdpleasing tasks, but can they hold down a traditional job contributing to the economy, like working on an assembly line or cleaning a house? When will Unitree G1 get a real job? Buying It in the US Jake Cooperstein, a 24yearold who lives in Miami, says he was inspired by Edward and other accounts to create a humanoid influencer of his own. In January, he visited the warehouse of a robotics shop in New York and tested the Unitree G1 robot. He was impressed by how easy it was to operate. The next day, he secured an order and paid the deposit. On Unitrees website, a basic G1 robot is priced at 13,500, but thats before any tariff, shipping, and taxes. A US distributor lists the robot at about 19,000 instead. Cooperstein was not satisfied with that, though. The most basic version doesnt come with more sophisticated parts like dextrous hands and is prohibited from modification. He instead chose the U5 variation thats designed for educational buyers. It has more parts and better customization but sits at the price of 66,000

Title: Americas Hot Hybrid Summer
Description: Gas prices are up, and US car dealerships are full of hybrids. Customers are going for it.
Content: In Europe, the rise in gas prices due to the Iran war has car buyers thinking about electrics more than ever before. Batteryelectric vehicle (BEV) sales were up more than 33 percent in the first ha 3445 chars
raw_full_content: In Europe, the rise in gas prices due to the Iran war has car buyers thinking about electrics more than ever before. Batteryelectric vehicle (BEV) sales were up more than 33 percent in the first half of 2026 compared to the same time last year, according to data published by European consultancies and nongovernmental organizations this month. The same has not happened in the US. Electric sales are up by nearly 15 percent in the second quarter of the year compared to the first. But the overall number of EVs sold is still small. Theyre lagging well behind the optimistic projections made before the Trump administration reversed federal support for the tech, which included generous tax credits of up to 7,500, and before automakers responded by dialing back their own electric plans. Instead, the more noticeable sales boom has been in cars that use traditional fuel, but more efficiently: hybrids. Sales of cars that sip gas rather than glug are projected to rise 9 percent this year, according to Kelley Blue Book, while sales of cars overall are slated to dip by more than 2 percent. Fuel Efficient The price of oil has fluctuated following the continuing conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, and so have gas prices, which are now up 30 percent in the US compared to this time last year. That alone has Americans thinking about alternatives to the traditional gaspowered car. Hybrids are more fuelefficient because they combine internal combustion engines with electric motors. Some plug in and use smaller gas tanks to move once their electric charge has run out; most dont, depending on technology thats decades older. But gas prices arent totally responsible for the USs hot hybrid summer, analysts say. Hybrids are more available than they used to be. They are, on average, more expensive than gaspowered cars, but not by much. And they dont give Americans range anxiety in the way that pure batterypowered cars do. Now the vehiclesonce viewed as a bridge between gas and electricwill likely stick around for the long haul. A hybrid doesnt feel like an electric vehiclethese are very different animals, says Stephanie Brinley, the associate director of AutoIntelligence at Mobility Global. People are looking to save; they have range anxiety. The hybrid is the perfect solution, says Karl Brauer, an executive analyst at iSeeCars.com. Hybrids still have a long life ahead of them. Unlike electrics, which tend to confuse Americans right now, hybrids arent as alien. More buyers thinking about hybrids isnt necessarily bad for EV adoption, Brinley argues. When buyers say, Ill look at this hybrid, thats opening up a willingness to consider something thats not traditional. Its a little crack in the armor that can make a difference when they come back to the market, she says. The American fondness for hybrids is another way US cars are looking really different from their global counterparts. Toyotathon This years jump in US hybrid sales has a lot to do with one automaker: Toyota. The Japanese automaker made its initial bets in hybrid tech back in the late 1990s, with the birth of the Prius. By the early 2000s, its hybrid system had made its way into other massmarket cars, like the Camry. And then, critically, Toyota stuck with hybrids as other automakers went allin on electrics in the 2010s and early 2020s. Now, US customers can buy a hybrid version of nearly every car in its lineup. Whats more, many of the automakers most popular vehicles, including the Camry and the RAV4, are now hybridonly. So maybe its unsurprising: This quarter, Toyota reported its hybrid sales were up by nearly 20 percent

Title: The Delicate Art of Making a 1907 House Smarter
Description: What happened when I introduced smart locks, automatic toilets, connected sprinklers, and a selfcleaning litter box to a historic home.
Content: At the very end of 2025, my wife and I bought our first home, a 1907 Craftsman in the heart of Portland, Oregon. Its a beautiful old house, listed on the National Historic Registry, and is largely un 2146 chars
raw_full_content: At the very end of 2025, my wife and I bought our first home, a 1907 Craftsman in the heart of Portland, Oregon. Its a beautiful old house, listed on the National Historic Registry, and is largely unchanged from the day it was built. This is exactly what we dreamed of in a house. Its loaded with history and vibes, mostly unmessed with across the decades. Were now simultaneously updating and restoring the home with a limited budget, big ideas, our own style, and plenty of sweat equity. The place we moved into was the level opposite of a smart homeand figuring out thoughtful ways to integrate modern technology into this old house without sacrificing aesthetics or ruining the vibe is the guiding principle. Were only getting started, but after a busy six months of learning, researching, and working cuttingedge technology into a house from the Roosevelt administration (Teddy, not FDR), Ive kept a running log of the tech choices weve made along the way. Today, our house is starting to feel simultaneously old and new, which is very much the goal. Its a lot of work, but I assure you its also a wonderful time. Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us. A Smart Thermostat Replacing the homes heating system was a day one fixour furnace was kicking off carbon monoxide and needed to be addressed immediately. We had a local furnace company in the basement before even moving in. But for daily use, we paired our spiffy new furnace with Ecobees new, midrange Ecobee Enhanced smart thermostat, which has a larger touchscreen than the basic Essential model and builtin radar for motion detection. In making this choice, I consulted WIREDs indepth review of the Ecobee, which prioritizes the units ease of setup and intuitive interfacethis made a strong case for selecting the Ecobee over other similar smart thermostats, like the Google Nest, which lacks the Ecobees presence sensors. The Ecobee gives us a monthly recap of our furnace usage and the average temperature in our home; walking into a low homeenergyscore environment in a home that lacks insulation and gets drafty, having this monthly recap has been helpful already. Many states have a smart thermostat rebate program through local gas and power companies, and right now were earning around 10 off each monthly bill for having a smart thermostat in the house

Title: CookUnity Prepared Meal Delivery Review (2026): ChefCentric Meals
Description: Ive tried most of the readytoeat meal delivery services in the country. CookUnity is the one that feels like real cooking, from real chefs.
Content: At a lower cost, each of Rajs delivery meals consistently tastes better than the (admittedly not great) Punjabi restaurant down the street from meless sugary, more rich, with saffrontinged basmati  2264 chars
raw_full_content: At a lower cost, each of Rajs delivery meals consistently tastes better than the (admittedly not great) Punjabi restaurant down the street from meless sugary, more rich, with saffrontinged basmati and chicken that remains juicy and plump, not overcooked. Rajs Indian gravies offer the most compelling argument for me to order CookUnity, in a city (Portland) where the best Indian food is often a halfhour drive into the suburbs. But, of course, Rajs meals are available only to those served by the Seattle hub. Others, near Los Angeles or Atlanta, may have other local chefs who offer similarly compelling arguments. I wouldnt know. Local Mileage May Differ CookUnity Beef Stroganoff with Truffle  Pappardelle from chef John DeLucie Photograph: Matthew Korfhage The strength of CookUnity is that each regional hub is basically local. But this is also a potential weakness: Each regional hub is different. Each hub has greater or lesser variety. Each also has a different selection of chefs and meals. But my good experience with the Seattle hub might translate to what youll find in a different kitchen, with different cooks. This may be true even if the same chefs name and face are on your meal box. Some chefs operate four or five kitchens at different hubs, and different kitchens may have different results, even with the same recipes. And heck, Ive had different results even from the same chefs. I can only speak to my own good experience and the good experience of my colleague Louryn Strampe, who ordered out of the Chicago hub. Note that while CookUnity offers a much bigger caloric range than most prepared meal kits, usually the big feasts are heavily carbloaded: rice, noodles, pasta. Those looking for a focus on proteins and veggies can find them easily, but usually in more moderate portions. Food cost is food cost. Starches are cheap. But I have reason to believe that CookUnitys other hubs also offer good cookingand that has a lot to do with CookUnitys business model. The overall factor that I think makes CookUnity work is healthy competition. Each CookUnity chef making prepared meals is, essentially, a competing food business within the same big commissary kitchen. Their name is on each box, and a good number of the chefs have restaurants and reputations to protect. There are many incentives to make each meal interesting and delicious. My experience bears this out. Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us

raw_full_content: When Auks original Mini 1 herb garden hit the market in 2024, it touched on something that many tabletop gardens had until that point failed to consider: If youre going to give up that much counter or table space, you dont want it to be for something ugly. Aerogardens and similar models look  fine, but youre probably not going to see one in the background of an Architectural Digest shoot. The Auk Mini filled that marketplace gap with its pairing of sleek Scandinavian design and utility, transforming the runofthemill herbgrowing operation into a conversation piece. When I reviewed the original Auk Mini last fall, I loved that it allowed users to plant their own seeds in widely available coco coir, an alternative to peat moss made from coconut husks. No proprietary pods, no subscriptions, no fussy app. When I started testing the brandnew Auk 2 earlier this summer, I wondered what new features could possibly justify a new model. Turns out, there was more room for improvement than I thought. Title: YouTube Star AboFlah Made Streaming His Life. He Wants His Kids to Live Offline
Description: AboFlah talks about his new goals, streaming for charity, and when its time to log off.
Content: AboFlah keeps looking directly into the camera. He cant help itthe YouTuber has collected 50 million subscribers and has spent most of his life streaming. For most people, a camera lens is intimidati 3171 chars
raw_full_content: AboFlah keeps looking directly into the camera. He cant help itthe YouTuber has collected 50 million subscribers and has spent most of his life streaming. For most people, a camera lens is intimidating and cold. For AboFlah, known as Hassan Suleiman in the few hours he spends offline, it is more comforting to look into it than to ignore it. We have our conversation in the studio of 8Flamez, the company he cofounded alongside Eyad Siyam and Saad Sarwar to manage creators and build infrastructure for the creator economy. Its a massive, whitewalled space scattered with props, furniture, and recording equipment, ready to film at any moment. He arrives on time but slightly annoyed at having missed an appointment earlier in the day. Hes not one to miss an appointment; or even an email, as I later find out. His inbox has a measly 17 unread emails. Online, he is frequently compared to IShowSpeed and KSI, both of whom he has collaborated with. But his defining moment goes beyond any clickbait; his charity livestream, where he spent 12 days locked in a glass box in Dubai, raised 11 million for refugees and broke two world records for the longest livestream video and the most viewers for a livestream charity donation event. Seated on a beanbag on the floor of his studio, he talks the way he streams: fast and unfiltered, in long unbroken runs that he occasionally interrupts to apologize for. He does this before, during, and after our conversation. At 50 million subscribers and with a company, a cartoon character on the way, and a target of 100 million subscribers ahead of him, he is thinking about what comes next. He speaks in Arabic, his speech threaded with the expressions of faithAlhamdulillah, Inshallah, Biithnillahthat punctuate many of his answers, and which Ive kept intact. CARLA SERTIN: Tell me about the cartoon youre planning with Spacetoon, Slayman. Why go with this concept? HASSAN SULEIMAN: I love cartoons a lot. Spacetoon  I was born and raised watching Spacetoon. So as soon as they proposed the idea of me being featured as a character, I loved the idea. I mean, its a really beautiful idea, so I took part. So now Slayman is coming out, Inshallah. I expect it will release on Spacetoon at the beginning of next year or at the end of this year. And Im very excited. I hope people like it, Inshallah. TV is very traditional media, and youre a streamer Yeah, it will be a new experience. But I expect, Inshallah, it will be a really great experience. Why? Because my audience is mostly young and loves entertainment. And Spacetoonand the character Slaymanwill be a beautiful story that conveys a beautiful and nice message in an entertaining way for the young audience. So, Inshallah, theyll love the idea. Look, TV is not like social media; its different. Thats why I refused to go into acting, because I dont really like acting that much. I refused things like, for example, being a TV presenter or doing a specific program and following the TV system. Because on social media, its much more relaxed. More spontaneous. Youre more yourself. You can do any idea. If I wake up today with a weird idea, I can do it on social media. In TV, you need a lot of approvals, a lot of things; its complicated. I got carried away talking. Im going to talk a lot. Forgive me, I will talk too much. Stop me if you want to change this up

Title: Dyson V16 Piston Animal Submarine Review: Powerful but Pricey
Description: The Dyson V16 Piston Animal is powerful and packs a ton of capabilities, but its not the Dyson Id buy with my hardearned money.
Content: Before you start mopping, youll need to roll the Submarine head back and forth for 10 to 20 seconds to make sure its damp enough to work. Youll know its ready when you see consistent water trails. B 2122 chars
raw_full_content: The initial, earlyrelease V16 model I tested had some clogging issues, but Ive since retested a current version, and I didnt have the same problem. The V16 and its All Floor Cones Sense cleaner head had nice suction on my thick rug and bedroom carpets. Despite my having vacuumed the week prior, the powerful V16 still filled itself with dust and hair after covering two small bedrooms and a couple of stairs. The V16 did a great job overall, but testing it alongside the older (and cheaper) Gen5Detect proved the two models mostly worked equally. In some cases, the Gen5Detect even outpaced the V16, which had mixed results vacuuming sand, struggling to catch more than half on a thinner rug, and pushing some sand into a pile in front of itself on a thicker one. It did a similar thing with cat litter on my vinyl plank floors. A second pass with the vacuum caught everything, but Id prefer to see such an expensive machine get it right on the first try. Thats especially true considering cheaper vacuums, like the Shark PowerDetect Speed (430), did so with no problem. While I like the included Fluffy Optic cleaner head, you dont necessarily need it, since the All Floor Cones Sense head also works on hard floors. Whichever cleaning attachment you prefer, the builtin release on the vacuums tube makes it easy to switch cleaner heads without bending over. Still, when Im vacuuming on my top floor, where there are carpeted bedrooms and hard flooring in the hallways and bathrooms, I just stick to the All Floor Cones Sense head for ease. Its nice having a single head that can do a good job with both. Photograph: Nena Farrell The Submarine version of the V16 that comes with the wet cleaning head costs an additional 120, and if you need to mop, its worth the upgrade. The Submarine version of the V16 Piston Animal impressed me much more than I expected. When you use the wet head, the LCD screen switches to give you two modesBasic and Maxand I found the Basic option to be plenty powerful for scrubbing dirty stains on my LVP flooring. The V16 also pulls itself forward with this head attached, as it does with other Dyson wet floor cleaners, like the CleanWash. This feature makes the mop easy to push around. It could handle various stains with just a few passes, though problem areas I mopped earlier in my cleaning sessions needed more swipes (likely because the roller wasnt optimally hydrated yet

raw_full_content: My tote bag is more a mobile workstation than a carrier. On any given day, its hauling a 16inch laptop, noisecanceling headphones, chargers, my daily planner, a water bottle, and whatever gadgets Im testing that week. Plenty of leather totes look beautiful on day one, but far fewer are designed to hold up against the reality of transporting thousands of dollars worth of tech every single day. Thats why Leatherology surprised me. After months of rotating between the Mia Horizontal Tote, Transit Travel Tote, and Large Zippered Downtown Tote, I found myself thinking less about the leatherthough its undeniably excellentand more about how each bag has been intentionally designed to fit specific workflows. But the first thing you notice, of course, is that leather. Leatherology uses semianiline, drumdyed pebbled leather that is soft and supple, making it feel broken in from day one without being overly delicate. Courtesy of Leatherology Courtesy of Leatherology The hardware is clean, the branding is subtle, and the totes dont feel ostentatious, which I appreciate. These bags look expensive because the quality of the materials and craftsmanship speak for themselves, not because theres a flashy logo plastered on them. And if you want something more personal, every model can be monogrammed. As a tech reviewer, though, I find that aesthetics go only so far. What impressed me most about these bags is their functionality, which is something I cant say about many luxury bags. The straps remained comfortable even when I loaded the bags with bulky gear. The interiors are wellorganized, preventing cables and accessories from getting lost in a single, cavernous compartment, yet they dont feel overengineered. Each bag is sturdy and secure enough to protect your valuables. Courtesy of Leatherology Courtesy of Leatherology Built Better Than It Looks The Mia Horizontal Tote (330) is the most relaxed of the three and has become my goto bag for the weekend. Its wider silhouette is ideal for farmers market runs, shopping trips, or afternoons working from a coffee shop when I dont need my entire desk setup. My Kindle, headphones, a sweater, and small essentials all fit comfortably with room to spare. Two interior slip pockets kept accessories within reach, while the removable leather pouch became my designated home for my card holder and lip balm. The magnetic closure allows for easy access during everyday errands, but because it lacks a dedicated laptop sleeve or zippered top, I wouldnt use it as a work bag for my commutes. Thats where the Transit Tote (465) comes in. This is the bag that feels purposebuilt for work trips, where a personal item often doubles as your office. It features two exterior pockets, nine interior pockets, two zippered compartments, and a padded laptop sleeve that fits up to a 16inch laptop. I could separate chargers, travel documents, and toiletries into designated, wellorganized spaces. A hidden trolley sleeve slides over rolling luggage, and the zippered top adds an extra layer of security at airports. Between the short leather handles and longer shoulder straps, its also comfortable to carry through terminals without constantly shifting your grip. Plus, it feels much more heavyduty than the Mia Horizontal, whose straps I sometimes worry might give out when the bag is overpacked. Theres also a foldable bottom gusset with a removable support panel that helps the bag maintain its structured silhouette. During my testing, it fit comfortably under an airline seat, but its always worth confirming measurements with your specific aircraft

Title: Etsy Is In Its Flop Era, and Sellers Are Fleeing
Description: Once a quirky bastion of amateur vulva jewelry and pet portraits, Etsy is now deluged with massproduced goods and AI knockoffs. Some customers dont seem to mind.
Content: In 2017, Emily Olson, a stayathome mom based in Boulder, Colorado, started selling prints and custommade puppy portraits on Etsy. Her watercolors were simple and relatively cheapimages of saucer 3730 chars
raw_full_content: In 2017, Emily Olson, a stayathome mom based in Boulder, Colorado, started selling prints and custommade puppy portraits on Etsy. Her watercolors were simple and relatively cheapimages of saucereyed corgis and malamutes in minituxes, which she sold for 75 to 300 eachbut dog owners adored them: They were a labor of love, she says. In 2021, she says she made more than 40,000 off her Etsy store, and her YouTube following ballooned to 180,000 subscribers. But in 2022, she noticed something odd: Her sales started precipitously declining. Competitors flooded the platform, and she kept finding copies of her work on dropshipping sites like Alibaba, where they were advertised as original creations. Then there were the AIgenerated pet portraits, which were supplanting her listings in search results and selling for a fraction of the price. The most frustrating part, she says, was that the AIgenerated portraits were getting great reviews. People were like, Oh, this is the cutest image, I love it in my daughters bedroom. They didnt really know or care who made it, they were just eating it up, Olson says. In 2022, she says, her sales decreased by 30 percent, followed by 50 percent the following year. In 2024, Etsy officially announced that it would continue to allow AIgenerated art on its platform, provided sellers disclosed it as such. Frustrated with the policy and with her declining sales, Olson posted a video on her YouTube channel in January 2025 titled: Etsy Was Great  Until It WasntWhy Im Walking Away. Etsy doesnt align with my values these days, she says in the video. It feels like theyve just become another giant corporation chasing profits above all else. Once a quirky bastion of amateur vulva jewelry and twee crocheted dolls, longtime Etsy sellers like Olson are now migrating from the platform in large numbers due to their frustration with policies they feel are lax. Competitors are emerging. Fybe, for instance, a new online crafts marketplace, will open to vendors August 1. It explicitly prohibits AIgenerated content and dropshipping on the platform, and will rely on volunteer moderators and direct conversations with sellers to ensure all products are humanmade. Both buyers and sellers on Etsy are a little discontented, says Rachel Powell, the founder of Fybe. I figured if we could start a platform that has human moderation and only allows vendors that arent using AI or using dropshipping, then we could be filling a very real need in the community. On the subreddit rEtsyCommunity, there are dozens of threads from angry sellers griping about declining sales and the influx of what one user referred to as AIgenerated slop that isnt labeled as such. Every maker Ive talked to is basically screaming into the void about it, and Etsy doesnt seem to care, one post concludes. It isnt just massproduced mugs or Tshirts. Buyers have been inundated by AIgenerated product listings for crocheting patterns, hermit crab pools, even medieval suits of armor. Longtime vendors say the handcrafted aesthetics once prized by the platform are disappearing, thanks to a burgeoning market of online entrepreneurs promoting Etsy as a place for AIdriven side hustles. The whole AI side of things has really, really hampered Etsy for sellers, big time, says Chloe Rose, an artist and content creator who for years sold stickers and original watercolors on the platform. Viktor, a UKbased illustrator who has been on Etsy for 10 years, says his sales have decreased by 98 percent over the last year alone, thanks to people using the platform as an easy way to make a quick buck. People have learned not to trust oncetrusted sites like Etsy, because they are tired of seeing AI slop that is now infecting the site, says Viktor, who goes by his first name online for privacy reasons. Unfortunately, this has turned potential customers away from actual artists

raw_full_content: Electrolyte powders, dissolvable tablets, and trendy readytodrink waters have graduated from the pockets of athletes to one of wellnesss buzziest categories. And its a crowded market, worth an estimated 39 billion globally in 2025 and forecast to double within the next decade. Much of the growth has been fueled by wellness trends and influencerfronted hype cycles, like Prime Hydration, created by YouTubers Logan Paul and KSI, which the company claimed pushed past 1 billion in sales in a single year. In other internet corners, dozens of celebrity and podcasteradjacent brands are all promising a means of optimizing your way to hydration. These products are marketed as daily essentials for everyonefrom office workers to gym regularspromising to combat brain fog, improve skin, banish fatigue, and aid recovery. Heres everything you need to know about the electrolyte obsession, and when these products are actually worth buying. What Are Electrolytes? Electrolytes are essential minerals, among them sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, and chloride, that carry an electrical charge once dissolved in fluid. That charge is what lets the body do much of its basic work, such as helping muscles and nerves work correctly. They work to ensure fluid stays balanced inside and outside every cell, as a serious imbalance can cause headaches, muscle cramps, dizziness, fatigue, and weakness. In more serious cases, severe electrolyte imbalances can interfere with heart function and require medical treatment. Who Needs Electrolytes? For most healthy adults, the body has been regulating electrolyte levels perfectly well long before trendy, flavored hydration sticks landed on supermarket shelves. In fact, if you eat a reasonably balanced diet and drink water when youre thirsty, theres a good chance youre already getting everything you need. The sachet earns its place in roughly three situations. Studies from the American College of Sports Medicine suggest that water alone is sufficient for exercise lasting less than an hour, but electrolytes become increasingly useful during longer sessions of prolonged, sweatheavy exercise, particularly in high temperatures or humidity. Theyre also useful for illness involving heavy fluid loss, which is why oral rehydration salts are a recognized medical treatment rather than a wellness trend. And you should also consider them during long stretches of fasting, when the food that usually supplies these minerals is absent. Are There Natural Electrolytes? There are many sources of electrolytes in everyday foods. If youre eating a reasonably varied diet (fruits, vegetables, lean protein, whole grains, nuts, seeds), your electrolyte stores are continually being topped up without the need for specialist drinks or powders. Research by the Beverage Hydration Index shows that milkbased drinks can maintain hydration for longer than plain water. The combination of protein, natural electrolytes and small amounts of fat slows the rate at which fluid leaves the stomach, helping the body retain hydration for longer. Coconut water too can replenish potassium. The Nutrition Source from Harvards School of Public Health notes that, essentially, any beverage containing electrolyte minerals may be labeled an electrolyte drink. Some are very costly yet only contain a small amount of these nutrients, while others may contain a high amount of only one nutrient such as potassium or sodium. Can You Have Too Many Electrolytes? For healthy adults, an occasional electrolyte drink is unlikely to cause harm. Daily consumption, however, can sometimes be counterproductive. Many electrolyte products contain significant amounts of sodium, despite the fact that most populations already consume considerably more salt than recommended. The World Health Organization estimates the global average of sodium intake a day is more than double its recommended limit and roughly 1.89 million deaths a year can be linked to excess intake. Regularly adding extra sodium may not be ideal for anyone managing high blood pressure or cardiovascular risk. Some formulations also contain substantial amounts of added sugar, making them nutritionally closer to soft drinks than health products. Anyone recovering from illness or sweating through an August shift outdoors has a fair case for supplementing. For everyone else, the best approach to hydration remains an unremarkable one. Electrolytes themselves are nonnegotiable. Electrolyte products are mostly just a lifestyle purchase. This story originally appeared on WIRED Middle East
